start_here: Say to your AI: "Add example.com to my Resend account in us-east-1 and show me the DNS records I must add." It runs tool:add-an-email-sending-domain.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of yours: it adds a domain to your email-sending account and answers the DNS records its owner must add; it changes no DNS.
instructions: 1. Connect your Resend account once so your key is held under the name resend-api-key; the key is never typed into the request.

2. Say to your AI: "Add <domain> to my Resend account". It calls tools:run with tool tool:add-an-email-sending-domain and {"name": "<domain>", "region": "us-east-1"} (region is optional: us-east-1, eu-west-1, sa-east-1 or ap-northeast-1).
3. Read the answer: the domain's id (keep it), its status, and records: each DNS record's kind, name, type, value and priority.
4. Add those records at the DNS host yourself; nothing here changes DNS.
5. Then run tool:check-an-email-sending-domain with the id, and read the result with tool:read-an-email-sending-domain.

worked_examples.title: Add example.com in us-east-1
worked_examples.ask: Add example.com to my Resend account and show me the DNS records.
worked_examples.given: Read from tools/email-sending-domains/tool-rows.json: the row POSTs https://api.resend.com/domains with {"name":"example.com","region":"us-east-1"} and your key in the Authorization header and returns Resend's reply unchanged; id, name, status and records are the fields its output_schema names. The id is the one test/list-email-sending-domains.test.mjs uses; the record values are synthetic.
